title: Empirically grounded needs model for the living population simulation
question: Which validated behavioral-science frameworks (Maslow's hierarchy, Max-Neef's fundamental human needs, Self-Determination Theory) and empirically grounded need-pressure/satisfaction dynamics should underpin the five needs (sustenance, rest, safety, social, purpose) and the scored decision model in NOXIA-LIVING-0001, and what plausible parameter ranges for need deltas, decay, and relationship trust/affinity change follow from the literature?
why_now: The living-population work is the current active effort (ADR NOXIA-LIVING-0001, migrations 20260825-20260828 incl. seed guard, diagnostics route app/api/game/population). The ADR specifies a scored decision model (need pressure + role obligation + local opportunity + relationship modifier - travel cost) and an acceptance criterion that 'Bedürfnisse verändern ihre Entscheidungen', but lib/game/population/engine.ts currently runs a tick%4 phase cycle with hardcoded need deltas (e.g. work: rest -0.05, purpose +0.04). Grounding the taxonomy and parameters in behavioral science would make the society simulation plausible and educational, and give KUEPER a reusable 'human needs' concept for future simulations.
